title: Tag Release
summary: Picks the next semantic version from commits since the last tag and prepares the annotated tag command for your approval.
description: Choosing a version number by feel leads to breaking changes shipped as patches. This command reads every commit since the latest tag, classifies them and proposes the smallest correct bump.
It writes the tag message from the real changes and prints the exact commands. It will not create or push a tag until you answer.
useWhen: You are ready to cut a release and unsure whether it is minor or patch
The team uses Conventional Commits and wants the bump derived from them
You need a short tag annotation without writing release notes by hand
You want a check that the working tree is clean before tagging
body:
Prepare the next release tag. Requested version, if any: $ARGUMENTS

1. Run `git status --porcelain` and `git branch --show-current`. Warn if the tree is dirty or the branch is not the release branch.
2. Find the latest tag: `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match "v*"`. If none exists, propose v0.1.0 and stop to confirm.
3. Read `git log <tag>..HEAD --format="%h %s%n%b"`. Classify: any "BREAKING CHANGE" or "!" means major; any feat means minor; otherwise patch. For versions below 1.0, breaking changes bump minor.
4. If the user gave a version, use it, but say so when it disagrees with your classification.
5. Draft an annotated message: a one-line headline, then bullets grouped as Breaking, Added, Fixed.

Show the bump reasoning with the commits that drove it, then the commands `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "..."` and `git push origin vX.Y.Z`. Ask "Create the tag?" Run the tag only after a yes. Push only after a separate yes. Never move or delete an existing tag.

example.result:
Last tag v1.4.2, 17 commits since. 2 feat, 6 fix, no breaking changes -> v1.5.0.

git tag -a v1.5.0 -m "Saved filters and CSV export"

Create the tag?

faq.question: Will it push the tag?
faq.answer: Not on the first yes. Creating locally and publishing are two separate questions.

faq.question: Does it work without Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads the commit text and diffs to judge impact, and says how sure it is when subjects are vague.

access: Reads git history and working tree status
Creates a tag locally, and pushes it only after a second approval
